turns.t: Morning, doctor. I'm Frank, and this is my wife Lorraine. We've come for the helicobacter retest, I hope that's the right word.
It is, Frank, nice to meet you both. You finished the treatment course, I see. Remind me what you took.
Clarithromycin, 500 mg, twice a day, I think, with another antibiotic and a stomach tablet, for two weeks. I'd have to check the box.
So 500 mg twice a day as you recall it. And how have you been since finishing?
The heartburn is much better, mostly, but still there in the evenings. A couple of weeks since I finished.
It's been a month, Frank. You finished on the fourth. I wrote it on the calendar.
So you say two weeks since finishing, and Lorraine says a month. I'll write two weeks to a month. Anything else?
A bit of belching, after meals. And I've been going off my food.
Any vomiting, or black stools?
No vomiting. No black stools.
Any trouble swallowing, or weight loss?
No weight loss, the scales say the same as always.
That's right, his weight's been steady, doctor.
Good. Any other health conditions?
High blood pressure.
Any bowel or stomach problems in the family?
His mother had a stomach ulcer, I believe.
And what do you do for a living, are you still working?
I'm a retired plumber. Thirty-five years.
Let me press your tummy.
Ow, careful. ~
A little tender at the top, but nothing worrying. Frank, the antibiotics only work if the bacteria are gone, so I'd like to check. ~
How do you check? ~
I'd like to arrange a urea breath test, but you must have stopped acid-lowering tablets for two weeks and antibiotics for four weeks before it.
I stopped the antibiotics a month ago, then. And the stomach tablet is the one I take every morning. ~
The stomach tablet must stop two weeks before the test, so I'd like you to stop it now, and book the breath test for two weeks from now.
Can he use anything for the heartburn meanwhile? ~
Antacid liquid when needed, but avoid spicy food, coffee, and late meals.
That I can do. ~
And if you vomit blood, pass black stools, or have trouble swallowing, come in at once.
We will. ~
I'd like to see you again in three weeks, once the breath test is done.
Three weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~
